tasks.title: Define client-authorized Run artifact ingress
tasks.objective: Establish the smallest generic capability and ownership contract that lets an explicit client materialize bounded opaque bytes on a Run host without giving ctxmux clipboard, image, Agent, or workspace policy.
tasks.outcome: The architecture cleanly separates caller consent and source policy from daemon capability, integrity, resource, storage, lifetime, cleanup, and Backend enforcement before protocol implementation begins.
acceptance: One reviewed ADR defines the artifact owner, ArtifactId and materialized reference semantics, local-native capability, request and result lifecycle, bounds, integrity, lifetime, release and cleanup policy, and every unsupported Backend or platform behavior.

The caller or embedding host exclusively decides whether clipboard, drag-and-drop, local file, generated bytes, or another source may be shared; ctxmux never reads, monitors, requests, or infers clipboard or user consent.

Daemon hard limits for size, concurrency, total retained bytes, file permissions, safe names, destination ownership, integrity, TTL and cleanup remain mandatory and cannot be disabled by caller policy.

Artifact staging and ordinary Run input remain separate generic primitives; an SDK may compose them, but the daemon adds no image paste, prompt construction, Agent identity, conversation, or terminal-rendering operation.

The trust boundary states that private owner-only files and non-disclosure protect against accidental exposure and unsafe modes but do not sandbox hostile processes sharing the daemon user's OS identity.

Wrong-case analysis covers partial uploads, disconnect before and after commit, quota pressure, stale cleanup, daemon restart, terminal Run races, unsupported Backends, misleading names, path traversal, symlinks, digest mismatch, duplicate ids, and uncertain client retry.

verification.proves: The reviewed owner, consent, capability, protocol, resource, security, lifetime, and non-goal boundaries are explicit before implementation.
Architecture links, wrong-case mappings, documentation consistency, and the ordinary repository Gate pass.

tasks.title: Implement bounded atomic artifact staging
tasks.objective: Implement the approved artifact-ingress protocol and one daemon-owned local-native staging path with exact integrity, bounded resources, atomic publication, and race-safe cleanup.
tasks.outcome: An authorized public client can stream arbitrary bounded bytes and receive a committed Run-host artifact reference, while every failure publishes nothing and leaves no unaccounted temporary storage.
acceptance: The Rust protocol SSOT defines capability discovery, bounded upload frames, opaque command or upload identity, declared length and digest, commit result, typed cancellation and error outcomes, release, and generated TypeScript parity without placing a multi-megabyte artifact in one NDJSON frame.

The daemon chooses all physical paths, rejects caller destination paths and unsafe logical names, uses a dedicated owner-only directory and create-new owner-only files, writes to an unpublished temporary file, verifies exact length and digest, fsyncs where the durability contract requires it, and atomically publishes before returning success.
Per-upload, per-Run, concurrent and aggregate byte quotas are enforced before unbounded allocation or disk growth; input backpressure cannot starve cancellation, release, stop, or daemon shutdown.

Partial, cancelled, oversized, malformed, duplicate, digest-mismatched, timed-out and disconnected pre-commit uploads publish no ArtifactId and leave no temporary file, descriptor, task, quota charge, or hidden retry side effect.

A committed artifact survives uploading-client disconnect for its documented Run consumption window; explicit release, terminal Run cleanup, TTL or quota eviction, and startup stale cleanup use one race-safe ownership policy and never remove a file still leased by a successful operation.
Unsupported Backend, read-only imported Run, terminal Run, invalid Run identity, capability mismatch, and resource exhaustion fail before artifact bytes are consumed or a file is created.

verification.proves: Protocol generation, TypeScript drift, parser limits, filesystem atomicity and permissions, cancellation, cleanup, quota, lifecycle and full repository regressions pass.
The public upload, commit, release, retry, lifetime, capability, error and unsupported-Backend semantics match the implementation.

tasks.title: Expose generic SDK and CLI artifact composition
tasks.objective: Make artifact staging usable by clean Rust, TypeScript, and CLI consumers while keeping clipboard consent and image-specific UX in the embedding client.
tasks.outcome: A client can stage a file or byte stream, obtain its committed reference, optionally send the path through correlated Run input, and release it without private daemon access or Agent-specific APIs.
acceptance: The Rust client and @ctxmux/sdk expose streamed file and byte staging, committed ArtifactId and materialized reference, release, typed errors, cancellation, and bounded local buffering through the public protocol only.

The CLI provides an explicit file-to-Run staging command with inspectable size, digest, artifact identity, materialized path/reference and lifetime; it never reads the OS clipboard implicitly or uploads a file merely because attach starts.

A client-side composition helper may stage then send the returned path, but stage success and correlated input success remain separate results so uncertain input is never replayed and an input failure does not falsify artifact commit state.

A clean TypeScript consumer supplies authorized PNG bytes, stages them, sends the returned path to a generic shell Run, and the child reads bytes exactly matching the original digest; arbitrary binary and fragmented non-UTF-8 fixtures use the same path.
A permission-denying host fixture issues no ctxmux staging request and creates no file, while a permission-allowing host cannot relax daemon quotas, permissions, integrity or cleanup.

SDK and CLI documentation shows how AgentMux or another host can bind clipboard or drag-and-drop policy without adding clipboard, image, Agent, conversation, Electron or React concepts to ctxmux packages.

verification.proves: Rust, CLI, TypeScript, clean-consumer, image fixture, generic binary, denial negative-space, correlated input and repository regressions pass.
Generic artifact composition, caller-owned permission policy, separate stage/input outcomes, limits, cleanup, trust boundary and unsupported behavior are documented.

tasks.title: Qualify artifact ingress under hostile lifecycle and load
tasks.objective: Prove the complete public artifact contract under adversarial bytes, filesystem races, disconnects, quota pressure, cleanup, restarts, concurrency, resources, and supported platforms before the capability is claimed.
tasks.outcome: Artifact ingress is a bounded, auditable Run capability with no silent partial publication, leaked secret file, resource escape, unsafe retry, unsupported Backend fallback, or image-specific correctness shortcut.
acceptance: Deterministic tests cover every frame and chunk boundary, invalid UTF-8 metadata, arbitrary bytes, misleading extensions, traversal names, symlink and replacement attempts, duplicate identities, length and digest mismatch, cancellation, disconnect, late frames, timeout, release and terminal-Run races.

Real filesystem fixtures prove private directory and file modes, atomic visibility, exact bytes, no partial reads, no orphan temporary files, no stale descriptors, startup stale cleanup, explicit release, TTL and quota eviction, and the documented client-disconnect lifetime on every supported local platform.

Stress and resource lanes cover many concurrent Runs and uploads, slow and silent clients, aggregate quota exhaustion, daemon shutdown, repeated cancellation and cleanup, with bounded RSS, descriptors, tasks, disk use and latency and no control-path starvation.

Retry tests distinguish pre-commit known failure, committed success, and unknown disposition; no SDK or CLI automatically resends uncertain artifact bytes or correlated Run input without an independently proven idempotency key.

Security review confirms that ctxmux never reads clipboard state, never accepts client physical destinations, never broadens same-user authentication claims, never exposes paths through unrelated Run responses, and documents that same-UID hostile child isolation is not provided.

A clean public-boundary qualification proves native happy path and explicit unsupported results for imported tmux, future remote, terminal and unknown-capability Runs; documentation and capability declarations contain no silent fallback.

verification.proves: Artifact protocol, platform, lifecycle, chaos, stress, security, resource, cleanup, SDK, CLI and clean-consumer qualification lanes pass together.
Every artifact-ingress invariant, gate, platform, resource result, trust boundary, unsupported capability and residual risk is auditable.
